sections.h2: Who values, bills and collects property tax in St. Charles County?
sections.html:
The job is split between two elected officials. One sets the market value of every parcel, and the other mails a single combined statement and hands the receipts to schools, fire districts and the rest. You will find both in the county Administration Building downtown, 201 N. Second Street, on a weekday schedule of 8 to 5.

  • Assessor Travis Welge: 636-949-7425 (real estate values), 636-949-7428 (informal hearings outside a reassessment year), 636-949-7420 (personal property).
  • Collector of Revenue Michelle D. McBride: Suite 134, 636-949-7470.
  • Payment website named in the county's tax guide: stcharlesmocollector.org.

Rates are not theirs to set. Each taxing body adopts its own levy, and the Collector's page says roughly 3% of what is collected remains with county government. Each parcel in the county falls under at least six jurisdictions: the state, the county, a school district, a fire district, an ambulance district and a library. Where you live inside the county therefore changes the total.

sections.h2: What makes St. Charles County distinctive for sellers?
sections.html:
Named for Charles Borromeo and organized October 1, 1812, the county takes in 593 square miles (560 of them land) of east central Missouri. St. Charles is the seat and O'Fallon is the biggest city. After the 2020 census only two Missouri counties were larger (Wikipedia).

Growth followed the highways. Interstate 70 crosses the middle of the county, Interstate 64 serves the southwest, and Routes 364 and 370 connect the suburbs with St. Louis County. The wedge bounded by I-70, I-64 and Route 94 was once nicknamed the Golden Triangle and is now called the Westplex, home to St. Charles, St. Peters, O'Fallon, Lake St. Louis, Wentzville, Cottleville, Dardenne Prairie and Weldon Spring. High schools sort into five districts (Fort Zumwalt, Francis Howell, Orchard Farm, St. Charles and Wentzville), and each district puts its own line on the bill.

QuickFacts estimates 426,499 residents as of July 1, 2025, living among 174,278 housing units. Four of every five occupied homes are owned (80.5%), and the 2020 to 2024 survey puts the typical owned home at $320,800, with households earning a median $104,692 and renters paying a median $1,370. Workers travel 24.5 minutes on average.

sections.h2: How is a St. Charles County home valued?
sections.html:
The Assessor estimates what each property would sell for on the open market as of the tax date. Real estate is revalued every odd-numbered year, new construction is added to the rolls annually, and personal property such as vehicles is assessed every year (Assessor page).

The office says it looks at several kinds of information:

  • Property type: residential, commercial, industrial or agricultural.
  • Structure measurements, checked against building permits and aerial photography.
  • Location data such as zoning, road access and neighborhood.
  • Recent sales of similar properties, leaving out sales far above or below normal market value.

An assessment is a mass appraisal built on statistics for groups of similar homes. It is different from a sale price, which is the amount a buyer actually paid, and from an appraisal, which is one detailed opinion of a single property made for a private purpose. If your value moved although you changed nothing, the cause is usually the market for similar homes. Assessment notices go out each April under the county's guide, and the Assessor's website carries a property database for looking up your parcel.

sections.h2: What are the St. Charles County payment dates and methods?
sections.html:
Statements for real estate and personal property are issued by December 1. Tax is owed by December 31, and anything received once January begins picks up the penalty and interest printed on the statement. An undelivered bill does not excuse the debt.

  • In person at the first-floor payment windows or the drop boxes at 201 N. Second Street. Cash is accepted at the windows only; checks, money orders and cashier's checks can go in the drop boxes.
  • By mail to the Collector at Room 134. Mailed payments count as of the postmark, and cash should not be mailed.
  • By phone on the toll-free tax payment line, 1-855-227-7840, with the bill number ready.
  • Online at stcharlesmocollector.org. If you use your own bank's bill pay, start it at least five working days before December 31.

Owners who cannot pay the whole bill can make partial payments before December 31, which lowers the late interest and penalty that would otherwise apply. The Collector also takes advance payments during the year. Lenders and tax services receive an electronic bill file for escrow accounts, but the owner remains responsible for the full amount.

sections.h2: How does a St. Charles County owner contest a value?
sections.html:
There are three steps, and skipping the middle one closes the door on the last. Start with the informal hearing, go to the Board of Equalization if you disagree with the result, and only then reach the Missouri State Tax Commission (county appeal page).

  1. Informal hearing with an Assessor's staff member, held from the end of April through early June. The notice says to schedule within 10 days of its mailing date. Useful evidence includes a recent sales contract, a licensed appraiser's report, comparable sales and photographs of defects.
  2. Board of Equalization. The appeal form must reach the county Registrar by 5 p.m. on the second Monday in July. In 2026 that was July 13 and it has passed; the next one is July 12, 2027. The board hears cases in July and August.
  3. State Tax Commission. The filing deadline is September 30 or 30 days after the board's decision, whichever is later. For a property bought after the second Monday in June, the deadline is December 31.

The Assessor warns owners to be careful about companies that charge a fee to dispute a value, since the data they use is public and available free from the office. An agent who gives valuation opinions in Missouri must be certified or licensed.

sections.h2: Is there senior tax relief in St. Charles County?
sections.html:
Yes. The Collector runs a Senior Real Estate Property Tax Relief Program for the primary residence of residents who were at least 62 and living in the home on January 1 of the tax year. You must apply or renew every year to keep the credit.

The program began with tax year 2024 and works as a credit against future increases. A person who becomes eligible on January 1, 2026 sets the base year with the November 2026 bill and should not expect a reduction on that bill. The credit covers every taxing jurisdiction on the bill, including schools and fire districts, but it excludes bond debt levies and the State Blind Pension Fund. Only real estate qualifies, so a mobile home taxed as personal property does not. The 2026 application window ran March 1 to July 6, 2026 and has closed (program page). Ask the Collector at 636-949-7470 when the 2027 window opens.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax if a St. Charles County house sells?
sections.html:
Whoever holds title at the end of the tax year owes that year's bill. In practice the title company prorates the current year's tax between buyer and seller at closing, and the buyer pays the full bill in December (county tax guide).

Before you list, pull your parcel from the Assessor's database and compare the current value with recent sales on your street. If the value looks high and the second Monday in July is still ahead, the appeal steps above apply to you. If you owe back tax, the Collector holds the county tax sale each August, a process required by state law, so clear any delinquency well before then. Ask the Collector for a current payoff figure and hand it to the closing agent.

sections.h2: Which dates shape the St. Charles County tax year?
sections.html:
Yearly rhythm of assessment and tax in St. Charles County
DateWhat happens
January 1 of odd yearsAssessor revalues all real estate as of this date
March 1Personal property forms due to the Assessor
AprilNotices of Real Estate Assessment mailed
Late April to early JuneInformal hearings with the Assessor
Board filing cutoff (second Monday of July)Appeals due to the Board of Equalization by 5 p.m.
AugustCollector's annual tax sale of delinquent parcels
September 30State Tax Commission filing deadline, or 30 days after the board decision if later
By December 1Collector issues tax bills
December 31Final day for penalty-free payment

Sources: the county's Assessor, Collector and appeal process pages and the Assessor and Collector guide.

faqs.q: Which office answers questions about a St. Charles County bill?
faqs.a: Call the Collector of Revenue at 636-949-7470 about bills and payments, and the Assessor at 636-949-7425 about value and classification. Both offices are at 201 N. Second Street in St. Charles and open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

faqs.q: Can a St. Charles County bill be paid in pieces?
faqs.a: You can pay part of it before December 31, which reduces the late interest and penalty that would otherwise build up. The Collector applies each partial payment to the base tax, interest and penalty and issues a receipt every time. Advance payments toward a future bill are also accepted.

faqs.q: When does St. Charles County reassess next?
faqs.a: Real estate is revalued every odd-numbered year under Missouri law, so 2027 is next. Notices arrive in April, and the informal hearing window runs from the end of April to early June. New construction is added to the rolls each year in between.

faqs.q: What if the Board of Equalization deadline is missed?
faqs.a: Missing it usually ends your appeal for that year. The county page warns that failing to file with the board blocks a further appeal to the State Tax Commission, except for newly purchased property. The deadline is 5 p.m. on the second Monday in July, which is July 12 in 2027.

faqs.q: Who covers the tax share at a St. Charles County closing?
faqs.a: Both, for their share of the year. The county guide says taxes are often prorated at closing and that the buyer then pays the whole bill at year end. Ask your title company for the proration worksheet before you sign.
